idea.text: Iron is more reactive than copper. When an iron nail sits in copper sulfate solution, iron atoms give electrons to the copper ions: copper metal coats the nail and iron goes into the solution instead. This is a displacement reaction.
idea.analogy: Like a stronger player taking a weaker player's place on the team: iron takes copper's place in the solution, and copper is pushed out as solid metal.

steps.title: Put on goggles
steps.instruction: Copper sulfate irritates eyes. Goggles on.

steps.title: 20 mL copper sulfate
steps.instruction: Pour about 20 mL of copper(II) sulfate into the boiling tube.

whatIf.order: Without goggles, one splash in the eye can cause serious, sometimes permanent, damage within seconds. That's why goggles go on before you open any bottle.
whatIf.rate: Fast pouring splashes the blue solution, which stains and irritates skin and eyes.
whatIf.overshoot: Too much solution won't change what happens, but the tube gets too full to handle safely.
whatIf.quantity: More solution means more copper ions, so the blue takes longer to fade. Less solution fades sooner.

explore.if: use a more dilute copper sulfate solution
explore.then: Fewer copper ions: the coat builds up more slowly, and the blue fades sooner because there's less copper to remove.

steps.title: Add the iron nail
steps.instruction: Lower the cleaned nail into the solution.

whatIf.order: Pour the copper sulfate in first so the nail has something to react with.

explore.then: Rust is a layer of iron oxide that stops copper ions reaching the iron, so the coat forms slowly and patchily. That's why the nail is sanded.

explore.if: use copper wire instead of an iron nail
explore.then: Nothing happens. Copper can't displace copper. You need a metal that is more reactive than copper.
Zinc is even more reactive than iron, so the copper coat forms faster and the blue fades sooner.

steps.title: Watch the nail
steps.instruction: Watch the nail's surface. Use the time-lapse to speed up.

explore.then: Particles move faster and collide more often, so the copper coat forms more quickly.

steps.title: Ten minutes later
steps.instruction: Fast-forward ten minutes and compare the solution's colour with the stock bottle.

explore.then: Much more of the blue fades, as long as there's enough iron left. The solution turns pale green from iron(II) ions.

safe-2.text: Drag the goggles onto your face icon.

vol-1.text: Enough liquid to cover most of the nail.

vol-2.text: Pour until the counter reads about 20 mL.

nail-2.text: Drag the iron nail into the boiling tube.

wait-1.text: Some reactions are slow. Keep watching the surface.

wait-2.text: Use the time-lapse control to fast-forward.

observations.whatHappened: A pinky-brown coat of copper grew on the nail, and over ten minutes the blue solution paled and turned slightly green.
observations.why: Iron is more reactive than copper, so iron atoms give electrons to Cu²⁺ ions. Copper metal comes out on the nail; iron goes into solution as pale green Fe²⁺. Fewer blue Cu²⁺ ions means a paler colour.

prompts.question: The pinky-brown coat on the nail is...
prompts.explain: Copper ions gain electrons and form copper metal on the nail.

prompts.question: Why does the reaction happen?
choices: Copper is more reactive than iron
Iron is more reactive than copper
prompts.explain: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its compounds.

captions.text: Copper sulfate into a boiling tube, then a clean iron nail.
captions.why: The blue colour comes from copper ions (Cu²⁺) in the solution. The nail is sanded so its surface is bare iron, not rust.
captions.safety: Copper sulfate irritates eyes and skin and is harmful if swallowed: goggles on, and wash your hands afterwards.

captions.text: Within seconds a copper coat starts to form...
captions.why: Iron atoms give electrons to copper ions. The copper ions become copper atoms, which stick to the nail as a pinky-brown coat.

captions.text: Time-lapse: ten minutes later the blue has faded.
captions.why: Each copper ion that turns into metal leaves the solution, so the blue fades. Iron ions (Fe²⁺) go in instead, and they are pale green.
